edges.description: Loss of RSK2 feedback inhibition elevates ERK1/2 phosphorylation and dysregulates Sp1-dependent transcription.
Loss of RSK2 kinase signaling perturbs craniofacial and axial/appendicular skeletal development.
Hyperphosphorylated Sp1 transcriptionally upregulates Gria2/GluR2 expression in RSK2-deficient cells.
Altered glutamatergic subunit regulation is proposed to contribute to impaired cognitive and neuromotor development.
Perturbed excitatory glutamatergic signaling may predispose neural networks to epileptic seizures.
Perturbed central synaptic signaling may contribute to paroxysmal startle-evoked motor circuit dysfunction.
edges.target: Stimulus-induced drop episode motor circuit dysfunction

edges.description: Disrupted neurodevelopment produces global developmental delay.
Disrupted central circuit maturation produces intellectual disability.
Impaired central neuromotor maturation manifests early with generalized hypotonia.
Epileptic network hyperexcitability manifests clinically as recurrent seizures in approximately 15% of confirmed patients.
Non-epileptic paroxysmal motor-tone inhibition triggered by unexpected stimuli produces stimulus-induced drop attacks.

edges.description: Progressive vertebral dysplasia produces thoracolumbar kyphoscoliosis.
Abnormal sternocostal development produces pectus excavatum deformity.
Abnormal sternocostal development produces pectus carinatum deformity.
Postnatal skeletal growth retardation results in short stature.
Characteristic acral skeletal and soft-tissue remodeling produces broad, soft hands with distally tapered fingers.
Connective-tissue and periarticular laxity manifests with prominent joint hypermobility.
Altered craniofacial morphogenesis produces ocular hypertelorism.
Altered orbital and midfacial skeletal development produces downslanted palpebral fissures.
Characteristic craniofacial and perioral remodeling produces a thick, everted lower lip vermilion.
Progressive craniofacial skeletal and soft-tissue thickening produces coarse facial features with age.
Impaired craniofacial and odontogenic development leads to congenital missing teeth (hypodontia).
Hypodontia and maxillary arch dysmorphism produce widely spaced teeth.
Craniofacial and thoracic skeletal abnormalities predispose to upper airway obstruction during sleep.
Progressive kyphoscoliosis can compress the spinal cord and compromise neurologic function, leading to spastic paraparesis/paraplegia.

nodes.description: Elevated ERK1/2-Sp1 transcriptional activity increases expression of the Gria2 gene encoding the AMPA receptor subunit GluR2 in RSK2-depleted cells, suggesting an indirect role of RSK2 in modulating glutamatergic neurotransmission and potentially synaptic plasticity.

evidence.reference_title: Rsk2 Knockdown in PC12 Cells Results in Sp1 Dependent Increased Expression of the Gria2 Gene, Encoding the AMPA Receptor Subunit GluR2.
evidence.snippet: Our findings suggest an indirect role of RSK2 in modulating the expression of AMPA receptor GluR2 subunit and, therefore, in regulating glutamatergic neurotransmission and probably synaptic plasticity.

nodes.description: RSK2 physiologically exerts feedback inhibition on ERK1/2 signaling. RSK2 depletion causes abnormally elevated ERK1/2 phosphorylation and increased phosphorylation of transcription factor Sp1 (Thr453/Thr739) in neural-lineage cells and in Rsk2-knockout adult mouse hippocampus, altering Sp1-dependent gene transcription.
